eventMetadata.context_description: Recent National Weather Service forecasts for Dallas-Fort Worth, projecting a maximum of 99–100°F under sunny skies with light southerly winds and heat indices near 103–107°F, drove near-certain trader consensus on the 98–99°F bin. Persistent high-pressure ridging suppressed cloud cover and moisture, keeping conditions drier than September norms of 92.8°F, while model runs showed minimal day-to-day variability. Official observations ultimately confirmed 100°F, illustrating how small forecast revisions or station-specific readings can still shift resolution despite overwhelming pre-event market-implied odds above 99%.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Guangzhou Baiyun International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 6 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=zggg

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent cloud cover, high humidity near 80-90%, and moderate rain or thunderstorms forecast for September 6 are the main drivers capping Guangzhou's daytime maximum near the long-term average of 32.7°C. Official and ensemble model guidance from sources such as WeatherBug and local meteorological services converge on a high of 30–32°C, with limited solar insolation and evaporative cooling from precipitation suppressing further warming. Historical records show September 6 highs ranging from 26.9°C to 36.0°C, but current steering patterns and moisture influx align with the lower half of that distribution. Market-implied odds clustered tightly between 30°C and 33°C reflect this narrow forecast spread and the modest upside potential if rain clears earlier than expected.

eventMetadata.context_description: A strong cold front advancing across southeastern Brazil is driving the market's tight clustering around 15–16 °C for São Paulo’s September 6 maximum. The system has already lowered temperatures on the 5th and is advecting cooler, drier polar air behind it while sustaining thick cloud cover and periods of light rain or drizzle that limit insolation during peak afternoon hours. Official guidance from Climatempo, IPMet, and regional models shows daytime highs suppressed to roughly 14–16 °C under these conditions, well below the early-September climatological average near 23 °C. Minor differences among ensemble members hinge on the precise timing of frontal passage, residual moisture, and boundary-layer mixing, which explains why 15 °C and 16 °C outcomes dominate trader positioning while probabilities drop sharply outside that narrow band.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Forecast models from sources including the National Weather Service equivalents and European centers indicate a maximum of 9–10°C for Buenos Aires on September 6 under clear to partly cloudy skies and persistent southerly flow.** This stems from a strong high-pressure system and recent cold-air advection that has suppressed daytime warming, with overnight lows near 3°C and dew points remaining low. Historical September averages hover around 14–15°C, but current conditions reflect a cooler anomaly driven by the positioning of the subtropical jet and lack of northerly moisture return. Traders appear to assign higher probability to 11°C (61.5% implied) than most official guidance, likely reflecting uncertainty in afternoon mixing or minor model spread, while 9–10°C outcomes together command roughly 24% of the market. Updated hourly observations and next model runs will clarify whether modest warming materializes before peak heating.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Chongqing Jiangbei International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 7 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=zuck

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast models show a cooling trend for Beijing on September 7 driven by an incoming northerly flow and widespread cloud cover with rain, shifting trader focus toward 30–31°C highs.** 

Current conditions feature warm, mostly sunny weather near 31–32°C on September 5–6, but official guidance from sources like the China Meteorological Administration and international models points to northeast winds and 65–80% precipitation probability on the 7th, which would suppress daytime heating through reduced insolation and evaporative cooling. This aligns with the market-implied odds clustering near 30–31°C (combined ~60%), above the long-term September 7 average high of ~28°C. Key variables include the precise timing of rain onset and any breaks in cloud cover that could allow brief warming to 32°C or limit the peak to 29°C, with model consensus still evolving ahead of the event.

Persistent high pressure and seasonal warmth typical of early September in the Yangtze River valley have kept temperatures elevated above the long-term average of roughly 28°C, while low humidity and stable steering patterns limit cooling or convective disruption. Updated guidance ahead of the daily high will refine any late adjustments.

No major model disagreements or sudden synoptic shifts have emerged in the latest updates, keeping probabilities stable ahead of final observations.

**Recent model consensus points to a highest temperature of 12–13°C in Buenos Aires on September 7, 2026, driven by a shift to northerly flow that is gradually replacing cooler southerly air.** 

Forecasts from sources including the Met Office, WeatherBug, and Yr.no show daytime maxima around 12–13°C (54°F) under mostly cloudy skies, with light to moderate northerly winds and minimal precipitation. This follows a cool early-September period influenced by southerly winds, typical of early spring at 34°S latitude where polar outbreaks can linger before subtropical air masses strengthen. The pattern aligns with historical early-spring variability, though current runs suggest limited warming potential before the 7th. Traders appear to weigh these short-range model outputs heavily, resulting in the tight clustering around 13°C and 14°C outcomes.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=mpmg

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

markets.question: Will the highest temperature in Panama City be 33°C or higher on September 7?

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from global models indicate a typical wet-season pattern for Panama City, with daytime highs likely reaching 30–32°C amid high humidity, scattered thunderstorms, and variable cloud cover that can suppress peak readings. Afternoon convection often develops by midday, limiting insolation and differentiating outcomes near the 31°C mode: clearer mornings favor 32°C or higher while earlier or more widespread rain caps values at 30°C. Historical September averages hover near 29–31°C, and the tight market distribution around these levels reflects model spread in storm timing plus limited new observational data just 24 hours before resolution. Traders weigh ensemble guidance from GFS and ECMWF against the narrow historical range, with any last-minute shift in steering flow or moisture convergence able to tip the maximum by 1–2°C.
